body.en: The enhanced ACT Math test (from September 2025) is 45 multiple-choice questions in 50 minutes — about 67 seconds each — and a calculator is allowed throughout. 41 questions are scored; 4 are unscored field-test items you can't identify, so answer every one. Questions run roughly easy to hard, drawing on everything from pre-algebra to trigonometry.

body.en: Don't linger — flag a hard item and move on so easy points aren't lost. Backsolve from the answer choices, and plug in convenient numbers for variables when a question is abstract.

label.ar: ⏱ 3-Tier Pacing Strategy (45 Questions / 50 Minutes) (نظام اختبار ACT واستراتيجيات الحل السريع)

body.en:
• Questions 1–15 (Easy): Spend ~40 seconds per question (10 minutes total). Bank time early while building confidence.
  • Questions 16–30 (Medium): Spend ~65 seconds per question (16 minutes total). Watch for multi-step algebra and word problems.
  • Questions 31–45 (Hard): Spend ~85 seconds per question (21 minutes total). These feature advanced geometry, trigonometry, and novel combinations.
  • Final 3 Minutes: Check flagged items and ensure EVERY single question has a bubbled answer!
body.ar:
• Questions 1–15 (Easy): Spend ~40 seconds per question (10 minutes total). Bank time early while building confidence.
  • Questions 16–30 (Medium): Spend ~65 seconds per question (16 minutes total). Watch for multi-step الجبر and word problems.
  • Questions 31–45 (Hard): Spend ~85 seconds per question (21 minutes total). These feature advanced الهندسة, حساب المثلثات, and novel combinations.
  • Final 3 Minutes: Check flagged items and ensure EVERY single question has a bubbled الإجابة!

label.ar: ▲ Zero Guessing Penalty & 4-Choice Advantage (نظام اختبار ACT واستراتيجيات الحل السريع)

body.en:
• No Negative Marking: There is absolutely no penalty for wrong answers on the ACT. An unanswered question is guaranteed 0 points; an educated guess gives a 25% to 50% chance of a point.
  • 4-Choice Format: Enhanced ACT has 4 options (A, B, C, D) instead of 5, boosting blind guessing accuracy from 20% to 25%. Eliminating just one obvious wrong answer raises your odds to 33.3%, and eliminating two gives a 50% coin-flip.
  • Letter of the Day: If running out of time on the last 3–4 questions, pick one consistent letter (e.g., C) for all remaining items rather than alternating randomly.

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Test format & strategy)
label.ar: ◆ لماذا تعمل هذه الطريقة رياضياً — First-Principles اشتقاق (Test format & strategy)

body.en:
Why Successive Multipliers & Harmonic Average Speed Work: If a quantity \(Q_0\) undergoes a percentage change \(p\%\) followed by \(q\%\), the compound multiplier is the product of individual scale factors:

\[ Q_{\text{final}} = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p}{100}\right)\!\left(1 + \frac{q}{100}\right) = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p + q}{100} + \frac{pq}{10000}\right) \]

Notice the cross term \(\dfrac{pq}{10000}\): an increase of \(p\%\) followed by a decrease of \(p\%\) yields \(Q_0\bigl(1 - (p/100)^2\bigr) < Q_0\). Similarly, traveling equal distance \(d\) at speeds \(v_1\) and \(v_2\) takes total time \(T = \frac{d}{v_1} + \frac{d}{v_2}\), so average speed is the harmonic mean \(v_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{2d}{d/v_1 + d/v_2} = \dfrac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}\).
body.ar:

label.en: Worked Example 0.A — Back-Solving from the Middle Choice \((C / H)\)
label.ar: مثال محلول 0.A — Back-Solving from the Middle Choice \((C / H)\)

body.en:
When an ACT algebra word problem offers five numerical choices in ascending order \((A\text{ to }E)\), testing choice \(C\) first eliminates half the remaining choices immediately if \(C\) is too small or too large.

Example: If \(\sqrt{2x + 7} = x - 4\), choices are \(A)\;1, B)\;5, C)\;9, D)\;11, E)\;15\).
Test \(C (x=9)\): \(\sqrt{2(9)+7} = \sqrt{25} = 5\), and \(9 - 4 = 5\). Matches immediately!

question.en: On the enhanced ACT Math test (45 questions in 50 minutes), a student allocates 10 minutes to the first 15 questions and 16 minutes to questions 16 through 30. How many seconds per question remain for the final 15 questions, assuming 3 minutes are reserved at the end to check answers?
question.ar: حل المسألة التالية في (Test format & strategy): On the enhanced ACT Math test (45 questions in 50 minutes), a student allocates 10 minutes to the first 15 questions and 16 minutes to questions 16 through 30. How many seconds per question remain for the final 15 questions, assuming 3 minutes are reserved at the end to check answers?

solution.en: \(\text{Time spent so far} = 10 + 16 = 26\text{ minutes}\). Leaving 3 minutes for review leaves \(50 - 26 - 3 = 21\text{ minutes}\) for the final 15 questions. \(\text{Time per question} = \frac{21 \times 60\text{ seconds}}{15\text{ questions}} = \frac{1260}{15} = 84\text{ seconds per question}\).

question.en: In the standard \((x, y)\) coordinate plane, what are the coordinates of the midpoint of a line segment with endpoints \((-3, 8)\) and \((5, -2)\)?
question.ar: حل المسألة التالية في (Test format & strategy): In the standard \((x, y)\) coordinate plane, what are the coordinates of the midpoint of a line segment with endpoints \((-3, 8)\) and \((5, -2)\)?

hints.en: To find the midpoint \((x_m, y_m)\) of a line segment with endpoints \((x_1, y_1)\) and \((x_2, y_2)\), use the midpoint formula: \(x_m = \frac{x_1 + x_2}{2}, \quad y_m = \frac{y_1 + y_2}{2}\).
hints.ar: To أوجد midpoint \((x_m, y_m)\) of a line segment with endpoints \((x_1, y_1)\) and \((x_2, y_2)\), use the midpoint formula: \(x_m = \frac{x_1 + x_2}{2}, \quad y_m = \frac{y_1 + y_2}{2}\).

solution.en:
To find the midpoint \((x_m, y_m)\) of a line segment with endpoints \((x_1, y_1)\) and \((x_2, y_2)\), use the midpoint formula:
\[
x_m = \frac{x_1 + x_2}{2}, \quad y_m = \frac{y_1 + y_2}{2}
\]
Substitute the given coordinates \((-3, 8)\) and \((5, -2)\):
\[
x_m = \frac{-3 + 5}{2} = \frac{2}{2} = 1
\]
\[
y_m = \frac{8 + (-2)}{2} = \frac{6}{2} = 3
\]
Thus, the midpoint is \((1, 3)\).

Common errors:
- Finding the difference instead of the average yields \(\left(\frac{5 - (-3)}{2}, \frac{-2 - 8}{2}\right) = (4, -5)\).
- Forgetting to divide the sum by 2 yields \((2, 6)\).
- Reversing the \(x\)- and \(y\)-coordinates yields \((3, 1)\).
